title: Economic Impact from COVID-19 on Singapore
what_it_is: Economic Impact from COVID-19 on Singapore

sections.label: GDP forecast downgraded after outbreak
sections.summary: MAS saw no unusual declines in short-term capital inflows, and MTI downgraded Singapore's 2020 GDP growth forecast to -0.5% to 1.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Fortunately, these movements happened in an orderly manner and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has not observed any unusual declines in short-term capital inflows.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: As a result of the outbreak, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has downgraded Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast for the year from the original "0.5% to 2.5%" to "-0.5% to 1.5%".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The current baseline view is that GDP growth for 2020, as an entire year, will remain positive, but reduced to around 0.5%.

sections.label: Budget Statement support details
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance will announce more details on supporting companies and workers in the Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: More details on how we will further support our companies and workers will be announced by the Minister for Finance in the Budget Statement.

sections.label: New investments not affected
sections.summary: The current assessment is that new investments, being long term in nature, will not be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second question by Mr Desmond Choo with regard to new investments, because these are long term in nature, the current assessment is that they will not be affected.

sections.label: Tourism and China supply impact
sections.summary: Chinese tourists make up about one-fifth of total tourist arrivals, and companies relying on China for supplies or parts will be impacted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For tourism, for example, Chinese tourists currently make up about one-fifth of our total tourist arrivals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For companies that rely on China for supplies or parts, there will be an impact.

sections.label: Companies should consider other markets
sections.summary: Companies should not put all eggs in one basket and should consider other markets including ASEAN, India, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But going back to my earlier point, in my response to Mr Desmond Choo, we should not just put all our eggs in one basket.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, it is important that while we look at expanding our presence in China, our companies should also consider other markets, including the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), including India and even further away, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America.
